title: Mean-Direction Deflation Reranking for Metric Misuse Repair in Frozen Vector Search

contributions.purpose: Frame the training/search metric mismatch as a deployment-time problem for frozen vector search systems.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis of how inner-product search on embeddings trained with normalized metrics degrades on anisotropic embeddings via mean-direction bias and hub vectors.
contributions.evaluation: Motivated by Iceberg-benchmark evidence that on ImageNet-EVA02 (radial alignment 3 degrees) inner-product search gets <1% label recall vs 85% for Euclidean distance.
contributions.source_quote: We identify metric misuse as a deployment-time problem for frozen vector search systems, where the mismatch between training and search metrics causes severe quality degradation on anisotropic embeddings.

contributions.purpose: Repair metric misuse at query time without retraining, embedding postprocessing, or index rebuilding.
contributions.mechanism: MDDR: a reranking method that deflates the query's projection onto the database mean direction with an adaptive coefficient based on query-mean alignment, requiring only a single precomputed mean vector.
contributions.evaluation: Deployable as a reranking layer on frozen vector indices with negligible query-time overhead and no modification to stored embeddings or indices.
contributions.source_quote: We propose MDDR, a reranking method that deflates queries along the mean direction with adaptive coefficients, requiring only a single precomputed vector and no modification to stored embeddings or indices.

contributions.purpose: Quantify how much of the inner-product vs Euclidean retrieval gap MDDR recovers.
contributions.mechanism: Gap-recovery evaluation against the Distribution Normalization (DN) baseline on anisotropic and near-isotropic datasets.
contributions.evaluation: 48.73% gap recovery on ImageNet-EVA02 and 89.44% on BookCorpus, outperforming DN by 9.20pp on anisotropic embeddings.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that MDDR achieves 48.73% gap recovery on ImageNet-EVA02 and 89.44% on BookCorpus, outperforming the DN baseline by 9.20 percentage points on anisotropic embeddings.

contributions.purpose: Characterize when adaptive deflation helps over fixed correction.
contributions.mechanism: Comparison of MDDR vs DN across anisotropy regimes (ImageNet-EVA02 at 3 degrees radial alignment vs BookCorpus at 45 degrees).
contributions.evaluation: On near-isotropic BookCorpus MDDR merely equals DN, while on highly anisotropic ImageNet-EVA02 adaptive deflation gives substantial additional benefit.
contributions.source_quote: We show that MDDR's advantage is specific to anisotropic spaces: on near-isotropic BookCorpus, MDDR equals DN, while on highly anisotropic ImageNet-EVA02, the adaptive deflation provides substantial additional benefit.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Unlike Distribution Normalization (DN) which applies a fixed correction to all queries, MDDR adjusts deflation strength based on each query's alignment with the mean, providing stronger correction for queries most affected by the anisotropy bias.
Our work connects hubness to the specific problem of metric misuse in vector search, showing that mean-direction deflation provides an effective deployment-time remedy.
MDDR differs from these approaches by introducing adaptive per-query deflation coefficients that adjust based on each query's alignment with the mean direction.

Unlike these methods that modify the embedding space globally, MDDR operates at query time without altering stored embeddings, making it suitable for frozen deployments where index modification is impractical.

notes: Partial tie result explicitly claimed as a contribution: on near-isotropic BookCorpus MDDR only equals the DN baseline; the advantage is confined to highly anisotropic embeddings.
